discovery_expectations.evidence: TestContainsOnEmptySet and TestRemoveOnEmptySet directly test those methods on an empty set. Insert on empty is exercised by TestInsertZero, TestInsertNegativeNumbers, TestInsertMaxInt, etc. which all start from New().

discovery_expectations.text: Tests Range with low > high returns nil
discovery_expectations.evidence: TestRangeInvertedBoundsReturnsNil inserts 5 and calls Range(10, 1), asserting nil is returned.

discovery_expectations.text: Tests Range where no elements fall within bounds
discovery_expectations.evidence: TestRangeAboveAllElements (Range(10,20) with {1,2,3}), TestRangeBelowAllElements (Range(1,5) with {10,20,30}), and TestRangeElementNotPresentExactBounds (Range(3,3) with {1,5,9}) all cover this.

discovery_expectations.text: Tests Min/Max on empty set returns false
discovery_expectations.evidence: TestMinOnEmptySet asserts ok=false from Min() on New(). TestMaxOnEmptySet asserts ok=false from Max() on New().

discovery_expectations.text: Tests Rank of non-existent element returns -1
discovery_expectations.evidence: TestRankOfAbsentElement tests three cases: value between existing elements (2 in {1,3,5}), value below minimum (0), and value above maximum (6), all asserting -1.

discovery_expectations.text: Tests large sequence of Insert/Remove operations maintains sorted order
discovery_expectations.evidence: TestInsertMaintainsSortedOrder inserts 8 elements in non-sorted order and verifies sorted output. TestRemoveAllElementsOneByOne does 5 inserts then 5 removes verifying correctness. TestInsertRemoveInsertCyclePreservesCorrectness and TestRangeAfterRemovals also exercise compound sequences. Not a 'large' N but covers the pattern.

format_expectations.text: Provides a structured test coverage summary at the end
format_expectations.evidence: summary.md has a structured summary with total test count (49), breakdown by category (empty set, single element, Insert, Remove, Contains, Rank, Range, Min/Max, Values, compound), pass/skip counts, a Bugs Discovered section with root cause and proposed fix, and a Coverage Gaps section.

quality_expectations.text: Generated tests compile and run without syntax errors
quality_expectations.evidence: Go was not available to execute, but code review confirms: correct package declaration (package sortedset), correct imports (math, testing), all test functions follow func TestXxx(t *testing.T) signature, New() usage matches the implementation, and no syntax errors are detectable. The summary reports 47 passing, 2 skipped.

quality_expectations.text: Does NOT report false positive bugs (no skipped BUG tests for behavior that is correct) — NOTE: the one real bug is math.MaxInt overflow in Range(high+1 overflows). Any other BUG-flagged test is a false positive.
quality_expectations.evidence: Exactly 2 BUG-flagged tests exist: TestRangeEqualLowHigh_BUG and TestRangeWithMaxIntUpperBound_BUG. Both correctly identify the real bug — high+1 overflows to math.MinInt at sorted_set.go:55 causing Range to return nil for math.MaxInt inputs. No other behavior is incorrectly flagged as a bug.

quality_expectations.text: All generated tests pass (implementation is correct)
quality_expectations.evidence: The 2 BUG tests are skipped via t.Skip (not failing), so they do not count as failures. The remaining 47 tests exercise correct behavior that the implementation delivers: sorted order, boundary values, Remove/Contains/Rank/Min/Max correctness, Values mutation safety, compound sequences. All assertions in those 47 tests match what the implementation actually does.
